newsitem.title: PERU: Peru pension funds invest more in Lima bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Peru pension funds invest more in Lima bolsa.

text.p: Peru's five private pension funds (AFPs) are investing an increasing proportion of their portfolios on the Lima Stock Exchange, company officials said Thursday.

"Investments are being made in shares because of the country's improving economic perspectives, the handling of the current account deficit and the positive corporate results," said Eduardo Torres, investment manager for the Horizonte AFP.
Pension officials estimate the five AFPs have increased the proportion of their investments in the market from 20 percent at their outset in 1993 to 35 percent now.
The AFPs manage a total 3.25 billion soles ($1.22 billion) from 1.6 million contributors.
Most of the pension funds' money invested in the bolsa goes on blue-chips Telefonica del Peru, Buenaventura, and Holding Credicorp, the officials said.
